webResetRoute.detail:
TOKEN PATH: page.tsx:13-16 is a route entry only — `const { token } = use(params); return ;`. ResetPasswordScreen.tsx:30 takes `{ token }: { token: string }` as a plain prop (split out precisely so the unit test can render it without React `use()` Suspense mechanics — page.tsx:4-8). WHAT RENDERS ON LOAD TODAY: nothing is fetched. There is NO useEffect, no probe, no SDK call at mount. `phase` initialises to "form" (ResetPasswordScreen.tsx:32) and the component falls straight through to the form return at :100-134 — heading "Set a new password", two password TextInputs (New password :104-115, Confirm new password :116-127), submit Button :129-131. GARBAGE TOKEN TODAY: the form renders identically for a garbage, expired, already-used, or never-issued token. The token is inert until submit. handleSubmit (:37-70) does a client-side password-match check (:41-44), then POSTs `client.post("/auth/reset-password", { body: { token, password } })` (:56). Only in the catch does invalidity surface: `if (isApiProblem(err) && err.status === 404) { setPhase("invalid"); return; }` (:59-62). So the viewer types a new password twice, submits, and ONLY THEN learns the link is dead. That is exactly the LD-15 defect. INVALID STATE (:72-84), rendered inline, not a component: ```tsx if (phase === "invalid") { return (

This reset link isn't valid

It may be expired, already used, or mistyped — request a new one from the sign-in page.

); } ``` Phase union is `type Phase = "form" | "submitting" | "success" | "invalid";` (:28) — note there is NO "loading" and NO "load-error" member (claim has both). A page-load probe requires adding at least "loading" and "load-error" here. CLIENT CONSTRUCTION (:54-55): `const serverUrl = resolvePublicServerUrl(getAuthStore().getSnapshot().serverUrl); const client = new LoombreClient({ baseUrl: serverUrl.replace(/\/$/, ""), getAccessToken: () => null });` — built inline inside handleSubmit. ClaimScreen instead hoists this into a module-level `publicClient()` helper (ClaimScreen.tsx:65-68); a page-load probe on reset will need the same hoist (two call sites). STALE HEADER COMMENT — the lane MUST rewrite it: ResetPasswordScreen.tsx:10-15 states verbatim "this screen does NOT probe the token with a GET first (unlike /claim, there is no GET /auth/reset-password to resolve state from — the contract only has the POST). The form is always shown; a 404 on submit ... routes to the SAME generic invalid-link treatment /claim uses, at the point the server actually tells us something's wrong rather than guessing up front." This is a load-bearing documented design rationale that LD-15 reverses. TESTS: ResetPasswordScreen.test.tsx spies only on `LoombreClient.prototype.post` (:26 `postSpy = vi.spyOn(LoombreClient.prototype, "post")`); there is no `get` spy. Test :103-115 "INVALID: a 404 shows the same generic invalid-link treatment as /claim" asserts `/this reset link isn't valid/i`; :117-126 asserts a non-404 stays on the form. Adding a page-load GET will break every existing test in this file unless a `get` spy is added to beforeEach, because the new useEffect fires on every render.

This invite link isn't valid

claimInvalidStateComponent.reuseNotes:
Not verbatim-reusable, for three concrete reasons:
1. NO COMPONENT EXISTS TO REUSE. It is inline JSX in ClaimScreen's render body (ClaimScreen.tsx:172-184), reachable only through ClaimScreen's own `phase` state machine. A lane must EXTRACT it first (e.g. apps/web/src/components/auth/InvalidLinkScreen.tsx) and refactor ClaimScreen to consume the extraction — otherwise 'reuse verbatim' is impossible and the lane would produce a third copy.
2. THREE HARDCODED, CLAIM-SPECIFIC STRINGS. Heading `This invite link isn't valid` (:175) vs reset's `This reset link isn't valid`; body `...ask whoever sent it for a new one.` (:177) vs reset's `...request a new one from the sign-in page.`; CTA label `Go to sign in` (:180) vs reset's `Request a new link`.
3. CLAIM-SPECIFIC CTA TARGET. `router.push("/login")` (:179) is hardcoded in the JSX; reset's is `router.push("/forgot")` (ResetPasswordScreen.tsx:79). The router itself comes from the enclosing component's `useRouter()` (ClaimScreen.tsx:71 / ResetPasswordScreen.tsx:31).
The shared half — `<AuthScreen>` with no tagline, `styles.formHeading` heading, `styles.bodyText` body, a `variant="secondary" className={styles.submit}` Button — is byte-identical between the two and is what the extraction should freeze. Minimal honest prop shape: `{ heading: string; body: string; actionLabel: string; onAction: () => void }`. Both flows share the middle clause 'It may be expired, already used, or mistyped —' verbatim; only the trailing remedy clause differs. Preserve the existing copy exactly on both sides — the tests assert on it (ClaimScreen.test.tsx:132 `/this invite link isn't valid/i`, ResetPasswordScreen.test.tsx:111 `/this reset link isn't valid/i`).

serverEndpoints.detail: Request-reset. `@Post("forgot-password")` on `@Controller("auth")` (:154), `@HttpCode(HttpStatus.ACCEPTED)`, `@UseGuards(SurfaceRateLimitGuard)`, `@RateLimit("passwordReset", "ip")` (:399-401). Validates: unknown body keys → 422 (:414-419), missing/empty `identifier` → 422 (:420-422). When mail is configured (:427) it does BOTH lookups unconditionally (getUserByUsername + getUserByEmail, :429-432) and, for a real user with an email, mints a token and dispatches `password-reset` mail with actionUrl = `${publicUrl}/reset/${plaintext}` (:436-455) — this is where the /reset/{token} web link is built. Otherwise it burns equivalent work (:461-462). Always 202 with `{}` (:471). Anti-timing floor FORGOT_PASSWORD_MIN_MS=200 (:143, awaited :469). Error shape: only 422 (unprocessableEntity → RFC 9457 Problem) and 429 (Retry-After, via RateLimitExceptionFilter, :155). `instance` is built by `sanitizeInstancePath(req)` (:412).

Reset-submit — THE ONLY PLACE A RESET TOKEN IS EVER VALIDATED TODAY. `@Post("reset-password")`, `@HttpCode(HttpStatus.NO_CONTENT)`, `@UseGuards(SurfaceRateLimitGuard)`, `@RateLimit("passwordReset", "ip")` (:491-494). Order of work: unknown-key 422 (:505-509) → missing token/password 422 (:510-512) → password minLength 8 422 (:514-516) → argon2id hash (:518) → `resetPasswordViaTokenAndEmit(db, { tokenHash: hashPasswordResetToken(body.token), passwordHash, nowMs })` (:519-523) → `if (!result.ok) throw new NotFoundException();` (:525-527). Validation is INSEPARABLE from consumption: the db function does an atomic compare-and-swap UPDATE (packages/db/src/query/password-reset.ts:162-169, `WHERE token_hash = $hash AND used_at_ms IS NULL AND expires_at_ms > now RETURNING user_id`) — there is no read-only liveness path. On success it also sets the password, clears must_change_password, stamps password_changed_at_ms, revokes ALL refresh tokens, and emits `user.password-reset` (password-reset.ts:184-205). ERROR ON BAD TOKEN: a BARE `NotFoundException()` converted by the problem filter to the ONE shared not-found problem — documented verbatim at :486-489 as {"type":"urn:loombre:problem:not-found","title":"Not Found","status":404,"detail":"Not found.","instance":"/auth/reset-password"} — byte-identical for invalid / expired / already-used / unknown, and byte-identical to an unknown route at that same path (asserted at apps/server/test/not-found-envelope.e2e.spec.ts:244-252).

THE CLAIM-SIDE PAGE-LOAD VALIDATOR — the shape LD-15 says to mirror. `@Get("invites/claim/:token")` on a bare `@Controller()` (:185), `@UseGuards(SurfaceRateLimitGuard)`, `@RateLimit("claim", "ip")` (:355-356). Body: hashes the raw token with `this.refreshTokenService.hashToken(token)` (:359), `getInviteByTokenHash` (:360), then `isInviteClaimable({ claimedAtMs, revokedAtMs, expiresAtMs }, nowMs)` (:363-369). READ-ONLY — resolving the token does NOT consume it. Returns `mapClaimState(invite)` → ClaimState (:374). On any failure: bare `throw new NotFoundException()` (:371), the same shared not-found problem, with `instance` collapsed to the TEMPLATE `/invites/claim/{token}` by sanitize-instance.ts:28 so the raw token never echoes back. Mounted under /invites, NOT bare /claim, because bare /claim collided with the Next.js page route (header :348-353).

Claim-submit. `@UseGuards(SurfaceRateLimitGuard)`, `@RateLimit("claim", "ip")`, `@HttpCode(HttpStatus.CREATED)` (:378-380). Re-runs the SAME existence+liveness check FIRST, before any body validation (:396-410, `throw new NotFoundException()` at :409) — an attacker with a well-formed body learns nothing a garbage-body attacker doesn't. Then unknown-key 422 (:414-419), username-required-iff-no-preset 422 (:421-427), password required + minLength 8 422 (:429-437), LD-13b email absent/null/string handling (:439-449+). Returns TokenPair (201). `instance` via `sanitizeInstancePath(req)` (:394).

Context only — carries `passwordResetAvailable` (contract openapi.yaml:4993-4994), true iff mail is configured. /login gates the 'forgot password' affordance on it; /forgot and /reset are deliberately NOT gated on it (apps/web/src/app/forgot/page.tsx:8-13). Not a token validator; listed so the lane does not mistake it for one.

The ADMIN/CLI tier's HTTP twin — authenticated, admin-only, mints a temporary password + sets must_change_password. NOT part of the self-serve mailed-token flow and NOT token-based. Named here only so the lane does not confuse `AdminResetPasswordRequest`/`AdminResetPasswordResponse` (contract :4792, :4815) with the public `ResetPasswordRequest` (:4780).

Content `application/problem+json` → Problem (4595-4597). UnprocessableEntity is 4598-4602; Problem response 4568; Problem schema 4606.

tokenValidationToday:
RESET: validity is checked at SUBMIT TIME ONLY, and the check IS the consumption. There is no GET, no probe, no validity flag anywhere in the reset flow. The single validation site is packages/db/src/query/password-reset.ts:162-169 — an atomic compare-and-swap `UPDATE password_reset_tokens SET used_at_ms = now WHERE token_hash = $hash AND used_at_ms IS NULL AND expires_at_ms > now RETURNING user_id` inside `resetPasswordViaTokenAndEmit`, reached only from apps/server/src/session/auth.controller.ts:519-523 (POST /auth/reset-password), which turns `{ok:false}` into a bare `NotFoundException()` at :526. The db module exports exactly four reset-token functions (`invalidateUnusedPasswordResetTokens` :41, `purgeExpiredOrUsedPasswordResetTokens` :73, `issuePasswordResetToken` :98, `resetPasswordViaTokenAndEmit` :157) — NONE of them is a read-only 'is this token live' lookup, so even the db layer has no reusable primitive; a lane must add one (the natural shape: `SELECT ... WHERE token_hash = $hash AND used_at_ms IS NULL AND expires_at_ms > $now`, mirroring `getInviteByTokenHash` + `isInviteClaimable` in packages/db/src/query/invites.ts:316+). On the web side ResetPasswordScreen.tsx has no useEffect at all — the form renders unconditionally (:100-134) and `phase` only leaves "form" inside handleSubmit's catch (:59-62).

CLAIM, BY CONTRAST: validated TWICE, and never consumed by the check. (a) At PAGE LOAD — ClaimScreen.tsx:82-102 fires `GET /invites/claim/{token}` in a useEffect on mount, mapping 404→"invalid" and anything else→"load-error"; server-side that is invites.controller.ts:354-375, a pure read (`getInviteByTokenHash` + `isInviteClaimable`) that returns ClaimState and never writes. (b) Again at SUBMIT — invites.controller.ts:396-410 re-runs the identical existence+liveness check BEFORE any body validation, so a token consumed between the two requests still 404s, and ClaimScreen.tsx:148-154 routes that back to the same "invalid" phase.

THE ASYMMETRY IN ONE LINE: claim can afford a page-load probe because its liveness check is separable from its consume; reset cannot today because its only check IS the consume. Closing LD-15 therefore requires a genuinely new read-only path at both the db and HTTP layers — not merely wiring the web page to something that already exists.
contractChangeRationale:
TRUE — no existing endpoint can serve this, verified four ways.

(1) EXHAUSTIVE PATH SWEEP of packages/contract/openapi.yaml: the only token-bearing or auth/setup paths are /setup/state:99, /setup/first-admin:122, /invites/claim/{token}:167, /auth/login:233, /auth/refresh:261, /auth/logout:288, /auth/forgot-password:303, /auth/reset-password:345, /invites:967, /invites/{id}:1009, /admin/remote/tunnel/token:4140, /admin/remote/probes:4369, /admin/remote/probes/{id}:4398, /probe/{token}:4453. /auth/reset-password (345-380) declares `post:` and nothing else — there is no `get:`, no sibling /auth/reset-password/{token}, and no validity flag on any response. A targeted grep for `reset-state|reset/validate|validate-reset|resetState|getPasswordReset|reset-password/{token}|reset-password/:token` across all .ts/.tsx/.yaml/.md returns ZERO hits repo-wide — nothing unused exists to adopt.

(2) THE CLAIM ENDPOINT IS NOT TOKEN-TYPE-GENERIC. invites.controller.ts:359 hashes with `this.refreshTokenService.hashToken(token)` and looks up `getInviteByTokenHash` against `user_invites`; reset tokens are hashed by a DIFFERENT function, `hashPasswordResetToken` in apps/server/src/session/reset-token.ts:28, and stored in a DIFFERENT table, `password_reset_tokens`. (Both happen to be SHA-256 hex — reset-token.ts:5-16 says so explicitly — but they are separate tables with separate liveness predicates, so a reset token submitted to GET /invites/claim/{token} simply 404s.) Likewise /probe/{token} (openapi.yaml:4453, apps/server/src/remote/probe-page.controller.ts) is probe-token-only and returns text/html.

(3) NO SERVER ROUTE EXISTS. Every `@Get(` in session/, invites/, and setup/ enumerated: system.controller.ts:60 capabilities; restricted-zone.controller.ts:248/263/281/292/303/319/330/349/365/388; restricted.controller.ts:165 count; users-me.controller.ts:94 restricted; invites.controller.ts:318 invites, :354 invites/claim/:token; setup.controller.ts:157 state. Nothing reset-token-shaped.

(4) NO DB PRIMITIVE EXISTS. packages/db/src/query/password-reset.ts exports only issue/invalidate/purge/consume (lines 41, 73, 98, 157); there is no read-only liveness query, so nothing could be wired up even at the service layer.

=== NON-CONTRACT EDITS THE SAME LANE MUST MAKE (a new GET with a token PATH SEGMENT touches five gate-enforced registries) ===
A. apps/server/src/gateway/auth.guard.ts — the literal `PUBLIC_ROUTES` Set (:51-60) CANNOT match a dynamic segment; add to `PUBLIC_ROUTE_PATTERNS` (:104-108), e.g. `{ method: "GET", pattern: /^\/auth\/reset-password\/[^/]+$/ }`. Without this the guard 401s the probe and /reset can never distinguish invalid from unauthenticated.
B. apps/server/src/gateway/sanitize-instance.ts — add to `TOKEN_PATH_TEMPLATES` (:27-35), e.g. `{ pattern: /^\/auth\/reset-password\/[^/]+$/, template: "/auth/reset-password/{token}" }`. Without it the 404/429 problem body echoes the raw reset token back in `instance` — the exact F9 leak that rule was written to close.
C. apps/server/test/conformance.spec.ts — add the new operationId to `PUBLIC_OPERATION_IDS` (:209-229) AND to `implementedOperationIds` (:934-947). The unimplemented-allowance is EXACTLY ZERO (:231-236), so a documented-but-unregistered operation fails the walk outright.
D. apps/server/test/not-found-envelope.e2e.spec.ts — the byte-identical-404 family is asserted per-path (:214-231 claim, :244-252 reset POST, :254-259 probe); the new GET needs its own case asserting `expectNotFoundProblem(res, "/auth/reset-password/{token}")`.
E. docs/ops/remote-access/reverse-proxy.md — ALL THREE published proxy recipes route the reset API by EXACT path and would silently send the new GET to the web UI instead of the API: Caddy `@api path ... /auth/forgot-password /auth/reset-password` (:91), nginx `location ~ ^/(invites/claim/[^/]+|auth/(forgot|reset)-password)$` (:171 — anchored `$`), Traefik `... || Path(`/auth/reset-password`))` (:217 — `Path`, not `PathPrefix`). Prose at :54-77 also enumerates 'these four' public routes and states 'only /auth/forgot-password//auth/reset-password (the API calls those pages make) go to the API' — that count and sentence go stale. Editing this file TRIGGERS CLAUDE.md's Documentation Sync rule: `pnpm docs:build`, then `rm -rf "/Users/ozzy/App Development/Websites/Loombre/site/docs-dist" && cp -R docs/.vitepress/dist "/Users/ozzy/App Development/Websites/Loombre/site/docs-dist"`, then `npm run build` in that site/ directory, all in the same session.
F. packages/db/src/query/password-reset.ts — add the read-only liveness query and export it from the public barrel (src/index.ts), per that file's header :14-19 (auth-adjacent identity plumbing, no ViewerContext; apps/server may not reach into @loombre/db/internal — dependency-cruiser enforces this and `depcruise` is gate step 5).
G. apps/web/src/app/reset/[token]/ResetPasswordScreen.test.tsx — beforeEach (:26) spies only on `LoombreClient.prototype.post`; add a `get` spy or every existing test breaks on the new mount-time fetch.

OASDIFF RISK: NONE. A brand-new path item plus a new schema is purely additive; `oasdiff breaking` (gate.mjs:247) reports no breaking change. Do NOT alter the existing POST /auth/reset-password entry (345-380) — narrowing or re-typing anything there WOULD be breaking.
proposedOpenapiDiff:
# ── 1. New path item. Insert immediately AFTER the /auth/reset-password
#      block (i.e. after packages/contract/openapi.yaml:380, before
#      `  /devices:` at :382). Mirrors /invites/claim/{token} (167-199).

  # LD-15: the read-only GET twin of POST /auth/reset-password above,
  # shaped exactly like GET /invites/claim/{token} — so the /reset/{token}
  # web page can resolve a dead link AT PAGE LOAD and show the same
  # invalid-link screen /claim shows, instead of only discovering it after
  # the viewer has typed a new password twice and submitted. Anti-
  # enumeration is not a concern here (256-bit tokens — see
  # apps/server/src/session/reset-token.ts); this adds NO new rate-limit
  # policy and NO obfuscation beyond what the POST already carries.
  /auth/reset-password/{token}:
    parameters:
      - name: token
        in: path
        required: true
        schema: { type: string }
        description: The raw one-time password-reset token (never the hash).
    get:
      operationId: getPasswordResetState
      tags: [auth]
      summary: Resolve whether a password-reset token is still usable, without consuming it
      description: >-
        PUBLIC, unauthenticated (LD-15). A read-only liveness probe for the
        token in a mailed reset link: a 200 means the token is currently
        unused and unexpired, and NOTHING is consumed — the caller must
        still POST /auth/reset-password to complete the reset, and that
        operation re-checks the token itself (a token consumed between the
        two requests 404s there, same as it would here). Invalid, expired,
        already-used, and well-formed-but-unknown tokens ALL resolve to the
        shared not-found problem (see the `NotFound` response):
        BYTE-IDENTICAL across the four cases, and BYTE-IDENTICAL to what an
        unknown route answers at this same path — `instance` is this
        route's TEMPLATE, never the submitted token, so nothing in the body
        varies with what was probed. Same "invisible == nonexistent"
        posture as GET /invites/claim/{token} and POST
        /auth/reset-password. Rate-limited per `rateLimit.passwordReset`
        (shared with `authForgotPassword` and `authResetPassword`) — the
        policy that already governs this flow, not a new one.
      security: []
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The token is live — unused and unexpired, and untouched by this call
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/PasswordResetState' }
        '404': { $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound' }
        '429':
          description: Rate limited (per-IP, shared with authForgotPassword/authResetPassword)
          headers:
            Retry-After: { schema: { type: integer }, description: Seconds until the next attempt is allowed. }
          content:
            application/problem+json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem' }
        default: { $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem' }

# ── 2. New schema. Insert immediately AFTER ResetPasswordRequest
#      (i.e. after packages/contract/openapi.yaml:4790, before
#      `    AdminResetPasswordRequest:` at :4792).

    PasswordResetState:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      description: >-
        Deliberately empty, exactly like ForgotPasswordResponse above: the
        200 ITSELF is the entire signal (this token is live). Carrying any
        member — the account's username, the expiry instant, which of the
        four failure cases applied — would hand an unauthenticated caller
        precisely what the byte-identical-404 posture (E8/M12) exists to
        withhold. ClaimState carries presets only because a claimant must
        SEE them to fill the claim form; the reset form has no field to
        prefill, so there is nothing legitimate to put here.

# ── Notes for the implementing lane ──
# * Purely additive: `oasdiff breaking` (scripts/gate.mjs:247) reports
#   nothing. Do NOT touch the existing /auth/reset-password block (345-380).
# * The server route is `@Get("reset-password/:token")` on the existing
#   `@Controller("auth")` (apps/server/src/session/auth.controller.ts:154),
#   decorated `@UseGuards(SurfaceRateLimitGuard)` +
#   `@RateLimit("passwordReset", "ip")` — the same pair the POST already
#   carries at :493-494. No new policy key: "passwordReset" already exists
#   at apps/server/src/common/rate-limit.guard.ts:40 and
#   surface-rate-limiter.service.ts:123.
# * Handler body mirrors invites.controller.ts:357-375: hash with
#   `hashPasswordResetToken` (session/reset-token.ts:28), read-only lookup,
#   liveness predicate (used_at_ms IS NULL AND expires_at_ms > now),
#   `throw new NotFoundException()` on any failure, `return {}` on success.
#   It must NOT write — no consume, no used_at_ms stamp.
# * See contractChangeRationale items A-G for the guard, sanitize-instance,
#   conformance, not-found-envelope, reverse-proxy docs, db-query, and

All step names/commands taken verbatim from /Users/ozzy/App Development/Loombre/scripts/gate.mjs:165-185 and the package.json files.

1. REGENERATE THE SDK (gate step 1, gate.mjs:165 → runCodegen at :202-204):
   pnpm --filter @loombre/contract run codegen
   Runs packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs, which emits BOTH packages/sdk/src/generated/types.ts and packages/sdk/src/generated/paths.ts from a single parse of openapi.yaml. Output is deterministic (sorted path keys, no timestamps) because the drift check re-runs it. It THROWS on any operation missing an `operationId` (codegen.mjs:56-58) — so `getPasswordResetState` is mandatory, not optional. Never hand-edit packages/sdk/src/generated/* (banner: '// GENERATED — do not edit').

2. DRIFT CHECK (gate step 2, gate.mjs:166 → runSdkDrift at :206-208):
   git diff --exit-code -- packages/sdk
   Must be clean, i.e. COMMIT the regenerated generated/* files. (packages/sdk/package.json also ships an equivalent standalone: `pnpm --filter @loombre/sdk run drift-check`, which is `pnpm --filter @loombre/contract codegen && git diff --exit-code -- src/generated`.)

3. OASDIFF GATE (gate step 4, gate.mjs:168 → runOasdiff at :215-255):
   oasdiff breaking <git show main:packages/contract/openapi.yaml> packages/contract/openapi.yaml
   The script writes main's version to a temp file and shells out to the `oasdiff` binary; it FAILS HARD if `oasdiff` is not on PATH ('Install it with `brew install oasdiff`'). It passes only on exit status 0. A purely additive path item + schema is non-breaking, so this passes. To reproduce it standalone before running the gate:
   git show main:packages/contract/openapi.yaml > /tmp/openapi.main.yaml && oasdiff breaking /tmp/openapi.main.yaml packages/contract/openapi.yaml

4. CONTRACT LINT (runs inside gate step 10, `pnpm run lint` → turbo → packages/contract):
   pnpm --filter @loombre/contract run lint     # redocly lint openapi.yaml
   Also worth running directly while iterating on the YAML.

5. CONTRACT PARITY TESTS (inside gate step 12, `pnpm run test`):
   pnpm --filter @loombre/contract run test
   packages/contract/test/ holds event-schemas.spec.ts and four parity specs (admin-only-event-types-parity, admin-only-parity-diff, capability-backend-description-parity, settings-category-parity). None is expected to gate a new public auth path, but run it before the full gate.

6. CONFORMANCE (inside gate step 12, `pnpm run test`):
   pnpm --filter @loombre/server run test
   apps/server/test/conformance.spec.ts walks every documented operation. The unimplemented-allowance is EXACTLY ZERO — register the new operationId in PUBLIC_OPERATION_IDS (:209-229) and implementedOperationIds (:934-947) or this fails.

outOfScope: apps/web/src/app/claim/[token]/ClaimScreen.tsx: the same preset-presence question is asked with two different predicates in one file — handleSubmit uses `claimState.usernamePreset !== null` / `claimState.emailPreset !== null` (:117-118) while the render uses `claimState?.usernamePreset !== null && claimState?.usernamePreset !== undefined` (:214) and the same for email (:215).
